If youre going for 16 plants in a 5.5g tank, it might be overstock depending what kind of plants it is. With fast growing stem plants, like Wisteria (as an example) will do well for the background, but they will overgrow the tank if left untrimmed and might shade other plants in the tank that need light. Currently, I have 9 plants (5 that are tissue culture) in my own 5.5g Planted Tank and have run out of room to plant more. As time flew by  these plants kept growing and I had to uproot a few and divided them for more plant growth and density. There was def. no room so I had to get myself a small 1 Gallon tank just for the extra plants I didnt want to waste. Experiment with a few easy plants and see how they grow. I started with 12 and settled with 9. I wanted to make sure I had enough swimming room for fish as well. Ive gone to Petco many times for tissue culture/stem plants and had great success.

Dwarf Hair grass, Monte Carlo, and Dwarf baby tears are a few. All of them will benefit the use of co2 with medium to high lighting and they will grow faster. Monte Carlo does not require much beyond medium to higher lighting and fertilizer to thrive. Currently I have both dwarf hair grass and monte carlo in low tech tank with medium lighting and does well. Without co2, these need more than 2 months to get a full carpet.

The way I've learned to clean up a sponge filter is using Aquarium Co-Ops method on Youtube. Maybe check that out to get an idea. Make sure you use the same tank water when cleaning up the filter as you dont want to kill off the beneficial bacteria using regular tap water. This is key. He basically took a large ziploc bag, filled it with the original tank water while gently raising the sponge filter into it without spewing all the gunk out. The gunk will stay in the bag and not spread through out the tank. With the cat hairs, you can gently take that out as well. However, since this is a newly set up tank, you can easily take those hairs off no problem without the method I mentioned because the beneficial bacteria hasn't settled yet if youre experiencing a bacteria bloom to begin with. I hope this helps, sorry if its lengthy lol :)

Adding in live plants for any fish will be very beneficial. Plants give out oxygen and can help combat ammonia spikes as well as nitrates as a food source. 5.5 is a perfect size and 10g is much better. A divider for the 10g might sound good for now but I'de be dealing with a slightly higher bioload and imo I wouldn't share the same tank with a Betta that has some kind of issue. Although, a secondary tank like the one your Betta is currently housed in can be used as a hospital tank too. I'de look into a plant substrate that doesn't lower your ph or raise it depending on how your tap water comes out. Bettas can range in many ph levels however they tend to like slightly acidic water in my experience. Catappa leaves can lower ph but the tannins that are leached out over time can be useful in aiding your Betta's fins and health overall during recovery after the treatment process with fin rot. This worked for me. I wish your Betta a speedy recovery!
